units.name: Terror Drone

tier.basis: Built at the War Factory with no further tech; the wiki lists it as tier 1.

cost_band.basis: A little over half the price of a main battle tank.

mobility.notes: One of the fastest ground units in the game. It crosses water and can even reach submerged submarines.

body.notes: A spider-like robot. Although it comes from the vehicle factory, the game treats it much like infantry: it rides in troop transports and heals like infantry.

armour.notes: Very little health. Machine guns and snipers hurt it badly and electric weapons do ten times normal damage; melee animals and radiation can't hurt it.

armament.name: Dismantler Claws
armament.summary: Leaps onto the target. Infantry die in one strike. A vehicle gets the drone inside it and takes damage from within until it dies or the drone is removed. Aircraft can be infested only while landed.

armament.name: Electro-Stasis Ray
armament.condition: In stasis mode, switched with the mode toggle.
armament.summary: A long-range beam that pins a vehicle in place: it can't move, transform or deploy, but its guns still work. One documented exception, the Allied aircraft carrier, is shut down completely.

crew.notes: One player is the drone. While it is inside a host, the camera rides along with the host.

abilities.name: Claws / stasis ray mode switch
abilities.summary: Swaps between the claws and the stasis ray. It uses one at a time, so pinning and infesting the same target takes two drones.

abilities.name: Jump to the next host
abilities.summary: If its own damage destroys the host, the drone climbs out and can dive into the next vehicle. If anything else destroys the host first, the drone dies with it.

strengths.why: One of the fastest ground units, so it scouts, dodges and reaches vehicles before they react.
Can't be shot once inside a vehicle; the enemy has to repair, teleport or give up the host.
Kills infantry in one strike, even elite commandos who aren't shooting at it.
Crosses water and reaches even submerged submarines.
The stasis ray outranges most guns.
Cheap and quick to build, so losing one costs little.

weaknesses.why: Very little health: machine guns, snipers and electric weapons destroy it quickly.
The claws need touching distance, so it is exposed on the approach and can't reach aircraft.
One mode at a time, and the ray stops movement but not the target's guns.
Dies with the host if someone else destroys the vehicle first.
Electric weapons do ten times normal damage, and normal repair can't heal it.

countered_by.why: Neither weapon can hit aircraft in the air; its only answer is to hide inside a vehicle or a friendly transport.
Machine-gun and autocannon fire does extra damage to it, so anti-infantry escorts shred approaching drones.
Electric weapons do ten times normal damage to it.
Repair drones, engineers and repair stations strip an infesting drone out of the host.
Snipers pick it off from range, and some can clear an infested vehicle.

counters.why: Lone or unescorted vehicles, especially unarmed economy vehicles, die to an infesting drone unless they reach repairs in time.
Kills infantry in one strike if they don't shoot it first.
Infestation and the stasis ray stop a unit transforming or deploying, trapping it in its current form.

combos.why: A second drone, or any teammate with a pin, holds the vehicle still so this one can jump in.
A helicopter or amphibious transport carries five drones for a drop behind enemy lines, or launches them over walls.
Drones hold enemy vehicles in place while heavier teammates destroy them.

units.memorable: A tiny, disposable robot that hides inside the enemy's own tank: once it's in, you can't shoot it, so the enemy has to cure the host.
units.as_player: A cheap, very fast and fragile T1 pick with a tiny hitbox. Dive a vehicle to ride inside and chew it up, or hang back and pin it for your team. Aircraft and machine guns are its nightmare.

sources.title: Terror drone (Red Alert 3), Command & Conquer Wiki
Terror drone official profile (transcribed), Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.note: Transcribes EA's official unit profile; the original page is offline.

uncertain.note: No source gives the stasis ray's exact range or duration, or says whether it must be held on the target.
The full list of ways to remove an infesting drone comes from one wiki page; the official profile names fewer.
Sources differ on the claws' internal damage type (explosive against vehicles and sniper-type against infantry, or 'melee').

units.name: Hammer Tank

tier.basis: Built at the War Factory but also needs a Super Reactor, one tech step above the starting units. The wiki's War Factory list puts it in tier 2.

cost_band.basis: The standard price of a main battle tank in RA3.

mobility.notes: A little slower than the Allied main battle tank and not amphibious. Heavy enough to run over infantry, which is its main answer to them.

armour.notes: The toughest of the three factions' main battle tanks. Machine-gun fire does much less damage to it. Facing matters only mildly: side and rear hits do 5% and 10% more (game data on the wiki).

armament.name: 85 mm cannon
armament.summary: A fast-firing anti-vehicle gun. Poor against infantry and unable to hit aircraft.

armament.name: Leech Beam
armament.condition: In leech mode. Since patch 1.11 the tank must stand still to use it.
armament.summary: Reaches about twice as far as the cannon. Deals modest damage and repairs the tank while it stays on target. A vehicle that dies in the beam gives up its weapon.

armament.name: Auxiliary weapon port
armament.condition: Filled once, by a vehicle that dies in the leech beam; kept for the life of the tank and can't be swapped.
armament.summary: Empty when built. Holds one weapon taken from the dead vehicle, such as anti-air flak, an anti-infantry gun, a tesla coil or artillery. It fires alongside the cannon, one weapon at a time, and is silent in leech mode.

crew.notes: One player drives, fires and toggles the beam. A two-seat version could give the beam and the stolen weapon to a second player.

abilities.name: Leech Beam (mode switch)
abilities.summary: Switches between the cannon and the leech beam. Leeching kills more slowly than the cannon; it is a choice to heal or to loot, not to deal more damage.

abilities.name: Weapon salvage
abilities.summary: When a vehicle dies while held in the beam, whoever lands the kill, the tank mounts that vehicle's weapon for good. It works on friendly vehicles with force-fire. Structures and naval-only weapons give nothing.

strengths.why: The most health and armour of the three factions' main battle tanks; wins tank duels one-on-one.
Heals itself mid-fight with the beam, so it can stay at the front without a repair trip.
A stolen weapon can cover its own gaps, such as anti-air or anti-infantry, or add a big-unit gun.
The beam outranges basic defences such as small turrets.
Runs over infantry caught in the open.

weaknesses.why: Its cannon can't hit aircraft and is poor against infantry; without a stolen weapon it has no answer to air.
While leeching it stands still, kills slowly and its stolen weapon goes quiet.
The stolen slot is permanent, so a poor first steal can't be undone.
Needs an expensive tech building first.
Slower than the Allied tank and can't cross water.

countered_by.why: Bombers and gunships hit it freely when it has no stolen anti-air weapon.
Anti-tank infantry, especially ones that burrow or garrison so they can't be crushed, wear it down from cover.
Freezing or shrinking it takes it out of the fight and lets other units shatter or crush it.
The beam can't target the drone and the cannon barely hurts it, so a drone can get inside or lock it in place.

counters.why: Beats the other factions' main battle tanks one-on-one thanks to more health and steady damage.
The beam outranges basic defences such as small turrets.
Runs over infantry caught in the open.

combos.why: The official notes pair it with an anti-infantry walker to cover its blind spot.
An anti-air escort, or leeching a friendly anti-air vehicle on purpose, covers its weakness to aircraft.
Teammates soften a big enemy vehicle while the tank holds the beam on it; the tank still gets the weapon if someone else lands the kill.

units.memorable: A plain battle tank that loots: anything that dies in its beam hands over its gun, so every kill becomes a loadout choice.
units.as_player: A mid-tier brawler with a cannon for fighting and a rooted, long tether beam for healing and looting. Teammates soften big targets; you collect the gun.

sources.title: Red Alert 3: Leech Beam effects, StrategyWiki
Hammer tank official profile (transcribed), Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.note: Transcribes EA's official unit profile; the original page is offline.

uncertain.note: Sources disagree on what a few Uprising vehicles give when leeched (Pacifier, Reaper).
No source states outright that the beam can't target infantry; it is described as working on vehicles and buildings only.

units.name: Multigunner IFV

tier.basis: Built at the Allied Armor Facility with no further tech; the wiki lists it as tier 1.

cost_band.basis: 800 credits in the final patch (it moved between 700 and 900 during balancing), cheaper than a main battle tank.

mobility.notes: Outruns most ground vehicles. Not amphibious, and too light to run over infantry.

body.notes: No rotating turret: the whole car turns to aim (its Red Alert 2 ancestor had one). Each passenger type shows a different roof weapon, so the loadout can be read at a glance.

armour.notes: Light armour and modest health; it relies on speed and escorts.

armament.name: Multipurpose missile launcher
armament.condition: Only when nobody is riding inside.
armament.summary: Rapid light missiles that hit aircraft about three times as hard, and from twice as far, as ground targets. Good against aircraft and light vehicles, weak against armour.

armament.name: Repair tool (any engineer)
armament.condition: An engineer of any faction rides inside.
armament.summary: Replaces the weapon with a repair beam for friendly vehicles. It drives to damaged friends on its own, removes infesting drones and cures corrosion. It can't attack.

armament.name: Stun bark / roar (attack dog or war bear)
armament.condition: An attack dog (Allied) or a war bear (Soviet) rides inside.
armament.summary: Loudspeakers stun enemy infantry for a few seconds from twice the animal's own reach. Commandos are immune.

armament.name: Auto-shotgun (Peacekeeper)
armament.condition: An Allied Peacekeeper rides inside.
armament.summary: A close-range shotgun that knocks infantry back.

armament.name: Missile pod (Javelin soldier)
armament.condition: An Allied Javelin soldier rides inside.
armament.summary: Fires a burst of eight rockets, then reloads for several seconds. Turns the car into a tank hunter.

armament.name: Sniper rifle (Spy)
armament.condition: An Allied Spy rides inside.
armament.summary: Kills infantry in one shot and can fire on the move. Also hits terror drones, but no vehicles.

armament.name: Twin autoguns (Tanya)
armament.condition: Tanya, the Allied commando, rides inside.
armament.summary: The commando's own guns, mounted: shreds groups of infantry but can attack nothing else.

armament.name: Cryo beam (Cryo Legionnaire)
armament.condition: An Allied Cryo Legionnaire rides inside (Uprising only).
armament.summary: A single-target freezing beam that, unlike the soldier on foot, can also freeze aircraft out of the sky.

armament.name: Gatling gun (Conscript)
armament.condition: A Soviet Conscript rides inside.
armament.summary: A weak anti-infantry gun; one of the poorest combinations.

armament.name: Flak cannon (Flak Trooper)
armament.condition: A Soviet Flak Trooper rides inside.
armament.summary: Anti-air only, a little stronger than the Soviets' own flak transport, on a fast chassis that keeps up with aircraft.

armament.name: Tesla gun (Tesla Trooper)
armament.condition: A Soviet Tesla Trooper rides inside.
armament.summary: Kills infantry in one zap and hurts vehicles and buildings. Patches added a wind-up delay because it was too strong.

armament.name: Radiation spray (Desolator)
armament.condition: A Soviet Desolator rides inside (Uprising only).
armament.summary: The Desolator's own fast-ticking radiation spray, good for clearing groups of infantry.

armament.name: Piercing sniper rifle (Natasha)
armament.condition: Natasha, the Soviet commando, rides inside.
armament.summary: Kills several infantry in a line, but can't fire while moving.

armament.name: Infantry laser (Imperial Warrior)
armament.condition: An Empire Imperial Warrior rides inside.
armament.summary: An anti-infantry laser that is also fair against light vehicles.

armament.name: Anti-vehicle laser (Tankbuster)
armament.condition: An Empire Tankbuster rides inside.
armament.summary: A fast-firing anti-vehicle laser with long range; guides call it one of the strongest combinations.

armament.name: Shuriken launcher (Shinobi)
armament.condition: An Empire Shinobi rides inside.
armament.summary: Throws shuriken that kill infantry in one hit, slightly faster than the Spy version.

armament.name: Bow launcher (Archer Maiden)
armament.condition: An Empire Archer Maiden rides inside (Uprising only).
armament.summary: Arrows that hit both aircraft and infantry, with a little more anti-air reach than on foot.

armament.name: Psychokinetic blast (Yuriko Omega)
armament.condition: Yuriko Omega, the Empire's psychic commando, rides inside.
armament.summary: A mounted version of her psychic attack. The gain is mostly range, speed and protection rather than damage.

crew.notes: One driver and one infantry passenger. Proposal for a player version: the passenger's class sets the roof weapon and the passenger aims it.

abilities.name: Weapon changes with the passenger
abilities.summary: Loading one infantry swaps the missiles for a stronger, vehicle-mounted version of that soldier's weapon or role. Unloading brings the missiles back.

abilities.name: Evacuate
abilities.summary: Drops the passenger out; the car goes back to its missiles.

strengths.why: Outruns most ground vehicles: a cheap anti-air escort and rapid responder from the first minutes.
Empty, its missiles hit aircraft three times as hard and twice as far as ground targets.
Changes role mid-match by swapping the passenger: anti-air, anti-tank, anti-infantry, stun or field repair.
With an engineer aboard it repairs tanks in the field and pulls infesting drones out of them.

weaknesses.why: Empty, its missiles barely hurt armour.
A passenger without an anti-air weapon removes its anti-air ability, and if the car dies the passenger dies too: one kill for the price of two.
Can't cross water or run over infantry, and the whole car must turn to aim.

countered_by.why: Tanks shrug off its light missiles unless an anti-armour passenger rides along, and the heaviest can run it over.
A Hammer that leeches it to death gains its anti-air missiles, whoever was riding inside.
Pilot snipers and bribing spies can empty or steal it; the passenger is pushed out.
A drone inside it can only be removed by another engineer car or repair drones.

counters.why: Its default missiles are built for anti-air, with extra damage and range against aircraft.
With a sniper, commando, tesla or radiation passenger it deletes infantry while staying hard to catch.
With an engineer aboard it strips infesting drones out of friendly vehicles; with a spy it can shoot drones.

combos.why: Engineer cars repair the main tanks from behind; bring two so they can repair each other.
Ferries engineers to capture key buildings, then picks up anti-tank soldiers for the next job.
Every infantry type is a loadout: the team's infantry mix decides what the cars can do.

units.memorable: A cheap, fast car whose gun is whoever sits in it: the soldier you load decides whether it hunts aircraft, snipes infantry, kills tanks or repairs them.
units.as_player: A two-seat T1 runabout. Alone, the driver has a light homing anti-air pod. When a teammate climbs in, the roof weapon becomes a bigger version of their class weapon and they aim it. If the car dies, both players are thrown out hurt.

uncertain.note: Sources list Soviet and Empire soldiers as passengers but don't say how they normally end up in an Allied car (bribed soldiers, captured barracks or mixed teams).
Whether the Javelin version can also hit aircraft: one wiki suggests yes, the other doesn't say.
Exact numbers for most mounted weapons are not published; only relative strength is recorded here.
